hosting.//trailingSlash: The marketing routes are prerendered as dist/<slug>/index.html (scripts/prerender-marketing-seo.ts). The moment those directories exist, Hosting's default behaviour 301s /trust/eu-ai-act to /trust/eu-ai-act/ — so every already-indexed URL gained a redirect hop and pointed at a shape that disagreed with its own canonical tag. false serves the no-slash form directly, which is the shape the canonicals, the nav and the sitemap all use.

headers.comment: The SPA entry. A rule for '/index.html' alone does NOT cover it: candidates open /take/<id>, and the rewrite serves index.html at THAT url without inheriting the literal path's rule. It was max-age=3600, so a deploy took up to an hour to reach anyone who already had their link open, and until then they kept loading the previous build's asset hashes. Ordered FIRST because Firebase lets a later matching rule win, and /assets/** below must beat this one.
Hashed filenames, so the bytes at a given url never change. LAST so it overrides the catch-all above.
